summary:
Read-only observations made in fdev on 2026-10-30 while building the M0 launcher (FS.GG.Coordination#1087, merged 21170a25), which encodes them. Recheck live state before relying on them: lanes and units change constantly.

- cgroup v2 with cpuset cpu io memory pids enabled at the root; systemd 262; user@1000.service has Delegate=yes with cpu cpuset io memory pids. Its app.slice enables only memory and pids for its children, so lane scopes have no io.max file until systemd enables io there when a unit requests an IO*Max property. Whether that happens for user-manager scopes is Unknown until the first real cap readback (M1).
- Agent lanes are not only developer tmux-spawn scopes: transient run-*.scope units, libpod scopes, chromium app scopes and logind session-N.scope (Home SSH attach) all appear under user-1000.slice. Session scopes belong to the system manager, not the user manager, so capping them needs sudo -n systemctl, not systemctl --user. The fsgg-store-dev and fsgg-learn-qual accounts run their own tmux lanes plus fsgg-store.service and learn-qualification.service in their user managers (other users need sudo -n systemctl --user --machine=<user>@.host). No SC2 service unit runs; SC2 is mounts only.
- In-process subagents share their parent session cgroup, so drain cannot be proven by cgroup for a Root session; the launcher requires a Root drain attestation and refuses build servers or compilers inside exempt sessions.
- Inside the guest every virtio disk reports rotational=1 and scheduler none, so HDD versus NVMe cannot be inferred in fdev. The HDD-backed set comes from Home evidence (environment/fdev-bulk-hdd-shared-and-host-memory in .github) and is resolved per mount (/srv/v3-pool, /srv/bulk, /srv/sc2-reserved, the LEARN qualification filesystem) to whole-disk major:minor at runtime.
- Other users /proc/<pid>/fd are unreadable to developer, so a pool-writer census needs a read-only sudo -n helper; without it the result is Unknown.
- MemAvailable varied between about 20.4 and 30.2 GB across 2026-10-30 (32 GiB guest, agents running), so the 26 GiB admission is met only with lanes drained.
title: fdev cgroup topology for native windows: where lanes run and how io.max can reach them
